html:
Ablai Khan was a Kazakh khan of the 18th century, born in 1711, who rose as a warrior against the Dzungars and became khan of the three Kazakh hordes in 1771.

As a young man he fought in the wars that followed the Years of Great Disaster and was once held captive by the Dzungars. He played the Russian and Qing empires against each other, swearing loyalty to both while acting on his own. After the Qing destroyed the Dzungars he moved Kazakh herds back into the eastern pastures.

He is the great hero of Kazakh national memory, seen as the last strong ruler of a free Kazakh Khanate. His grandson Kenesary Kasymov led the last great revolt against Russia. A university and many streets in Almaty and Astana are named after him.
